articleTitle: Tackling Satisfiability: SAT Instances Classification Using Several Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The Boolean Satisfiability Problem (SAT) is a computationally challenging and fundamental problem in computer science, with extensive applications in cryptography, artificial intelligence, and hardware verification. This paper examines the application of machine learning techniques to categorize Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF) instances as either satisfiable (SAT) or unsatisfiable (UNSAT). We investigate a variety of models, such as Naive Bayes (NB), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), and Neural Networks (NN), by utilizing features that encapsulate the intrinsic properties of CNF formulas. We have demonstrated the high accuracy of these models' ability to predict satisfiability by conducting extensive experiments to analyze their performance. Our findings demonstrate that machine learning can provide a scalable and efficient alternative to conventional SAT solvers, thereby introducing new opportunities for the future to address intricate satisfiability problems.

articleTitle: An Efficient ECC-Based Authentication Protocol for Secure RFID Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: As Internet and Communication Technologies (ICT) evolve, RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) has become essential in healthcare for efficiently tracking and managing tagged medical devices. While RFID tags are extensively used on various healthcare assets, they are exposed to serious security and privacy risks, such as eavesdropping, data tampering, and interception, which threaten the confidentiality of healthcare professionals and patients. Despite the development of multiple lightweight RFID authentication schemes, many still suffer from vulnerabilities like replay, impersonation, and de-synchronization attacks. To address these limitations, we present a robust and efficient RFID authentication scheme designed specifically for IoT-enabled healthcare applications. By integrating Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), our scheme delivers strong security with a low computational footprint, ensuring resilience against all evaluated attack types. Comprehensive security and performance testing demonstrate that our protocol offers an effective balance of security and efficiency, making it an ideal and secure choice for real-time healthcare environments.

articleTitle: Data-driven Automatic Facial Image Colorization using an Encoder-Decoder Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Facial image colorization is a challenging task in computer vision, aimed at generating realistic and accurate colored versions of grayscale facial images. This study introduces a novel approach that leverages the power of an encoder-decoder network to predict and generate high-quality colored facial images from their grayscale counterparts. The proposed method surpasses other state-of-the-art techniques, showcasing promising and superior results. By harnessing the representation learning capabilities of the encoder-decoder network, meaningful facial features are captured, enabling effective inference of appropriate color distributions. This architecture facilitates realistic and visually appealing colorizations while preserving intricate facial details. Comprehensive visual comparisons with other state-of-the-art methods demonstrate significant improvements in color fidelity and overall image quality. Experimental results validate the efficiency of the encoder-decoder network in accurately predicting facial colors, even in challenging regions such as hair, eyes, and lips. The colorized images exhibit vibrant and lifelike tones, providing a faithful representation of the original grayscale images.

articleTitle: Using BPMN to Improve Quality Insurance in Algerian High-Education Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This study aims to explore the potential of using BPMN to improve quality assurance in Algerian higher education institutions, with a specific focus on the exam and assessment platform in the Department of Computer Science at the University of Mohamed Khider. Building upon the framework provided by the DIGITAQ project-a digital ecosystem for quality assurance in Algerian higher education developed under ERASMUS+-this research seeks to address the inefficiencies and challenges faced by these institutions. By developing and implementing a tailored BPMN framework, this study aligns with DIGITAQ's objectives of standardizing quality practices across higher education domains. The significance of this study lies in its potential to offer a practical solution to quality assurance challenges, particularly within the context of exam and assessment processes. This research not only fills a critical gap in the existing literature but also presents a framework adaptable to other educational contexts. The findings will contribute to the broader field of educational process improvement and provide valuable insights for policymakers, administrators, and researchers.

articleTitle: A Boosting Machine Learning Model for Predicting Student Performance in E-Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: In the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, e-learning systems have gained renewed importance. Researchers have focused on improving these platforms by addressing key challenges in MOOCs, with student performance being one of the most critical areas. The widespread use of e-learning platforms has generated vast amounts of valuable data, providing rich opportunities for data mining research. In this study, we aim to predict student performance and dropout using data from the OULAD dataset. The Boosting method was applied, utilizing machine learning models such as Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), Decision Trees (DT), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naive Bayes (NB), and Logistic Regression (LR). After experimenting with various approaches, Random Forest achieved the best performance with F1-scores of 86%, 81%, and 93% for the Dropout, Fail, and Pass classes, respectively.

articleTitle: Bridging the Gap: Transfer Learning for Dialect Identification in Low-Resource Settings A Case Study with Algerian Arabic
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This paper explores bridging the gap between well- resourced languages and low-resource languages in Natural Language Processing (NLP). We investigate leveraging Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) as a source for transferring knowledge to a low-resource dialect, Algerian Arabic, for the task of dialect identification. We compare the performance of three pre-trained models: AraBERT, DziriBERT, and mBERT. Our evaluation uses the Madar Corpus, a collection of parallel sentences from various languages and dialects. For this study, we focus on the Algerian Arabic and their corresponding MSA counterparts, comprising a dataset of 4k sentences. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of transferring knowledge from MSA and other well-resourced languages to enhance NLP tasks for low-resource languages.

articleTitle: Prognostics of the Lithium-Ion Battery Based on Deep Learning Algorithms: Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Precise predictions of the remaining useful life (RUL) of batteries are becoming increasingly vital in intelligent battery health management systems. Progress in deep learning offers novel data-driven methodologies to address this issue. This paper presents a comprehensive deep learning methodology for forecasting the remaining useful life of batteries through the utilization of deep neural networks (DNNs). Initially, data are acquired from the NASA Li-batteries. A deep neural network is trained using the remaining useful life prediction model for batteries. This methodology is utilized across multiple deep learning models, and the comparative analysis of the results indicates that the CNN-LSTM model yields superior accuracy, necessitating further efforts to enhance these models for improved remaining useful life prediction.

articleTitle: Parallel TLBO Framework for Structuring Elements Optimization in VHR Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of structuring elements in classification of very high resolution (VHR) image through mathematical morphology (MM). Indeed, the standard SEs are not suitable for the classification of VHR images from urban regions in which the spatial features are very complex and vary in shapes and sizes. Therefore, perceiving systematically the best layout of the structuring element (SE) to VHR image classification is an accelerated research subject. The aim of this paper is to propose an adaptive parallel teaching-learning based optimization (PTLBO) framework that is able to work out a unique SE whose configuration is optimal and non-fixed, which may change adaptively in conformity with the formats of the features and the classification duty. The proposed optimization framework is made independent of any algorithm-specific parameters and not constrained by using a finite quantity of SEs in the classification. Moreover, a cascade SVM (CSVM) classifier is adopted in this work during the phase of classifying the morphological features in order to achieve the highest classification results within the desired time. Finally, the experimental tests are performed in order to validate the efficacy of the proposed PTLBO framework, and the comparative results reveal the advantages of the presented approach in contrast to the prior works.

articleTitle: A Survey of Deep Learning Solutions for Network Routing in Modern Networks: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The rise of data-driven networks and emerging technologies like the Internet of Things (IoT) and Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs) has intensified research on optimizing routing mechanisms. Traditional protocols often struggle with the scalability and adaptability demands of modern networks. Deep Learning (DL) techniques, including Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), offer promising solutions by enabling real-time adaptive routing. This survey reviews state-of-the-art DL-based routing approaches, highlighting their strengths and research directions. Findings suggest that models like RNNs, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), and DRL can significantly enhance routing efficiency in dynamic, large-scale networks.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Real-Time Data Acquisition and Transmission Using Ethernet UDP: Application of MCSA for Induction Motor Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: In industrial applications, using Ethernet for data communication has become increasingly important due to its high speed, reliability, and ability to handle large volumes of data. This paper presents the development of a real-time data acquisition and transmission system utilizing FPGA technology and Ethernet UDP protocol, designed explicitly for Motor Current Signature Analysis (MCSA) in induction motor diagnosis. The system incorporates an external ADC (AD7606) for high-precision data acquisition controlled by an FPGA architecture. The acquired data is then transmitted to a PC via an Ethernet module (W5500) using the UDP protocol. A user-friendly graphical user interface (GUI) is developed to display the results, facilitating real-time monitoring and analysis. This implementation provides an efficient and reliable solution for real-time motor current signature analysis, enabling accurate diagnosis of various induction motor faults through MCSA. Experimental results validate the system's effectiveness in accurately diagnosing induction motor faults.

articleTitle: Automatic Blood Vessel Segmentation using Magnitude Images from Magnetic Resonance Elastography
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Quantifying hepatic stiffness through Magnetic Resonance Elastography (MRE) is essential for assessing liver health, yet it remains a complex task, due to the need for precise region of interest (ROI) placement. This process requires ROIs to be positioned in areas free from blood vessels as their presence can distort stiffness measurements. However, the poor quality of magnitude images often degraded by motion artefacts due to vibrations in the MRE process, makes manual placement challenging. To address this, our study aims to develop an automatic method for hepatic blood vessel detection using a Deep Learning (DL) model. We employed a 2D U-Net architecture for vessel segmentation, designed to differentiate blood vessels from liver tissue in MRE magnitude images affected by artefacts. The accuracy of the 2D U-Net segmentation was quantitatively evaluated using two primary metrics: the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and the Hausdorff Distance (HD). Our proposed algorithm achieved high performance, with a high DSC indicating reliable segmentation overlap and a low HD reflecting precise boundary delineation. This AI based method demonstrates a great potential for improving the accuracy of hepatic stiffness quantification, providing a consistent and efficient alternative to manual vessel exclusion. By ensuring precise blood vessel detection

articleTitle: A Federated Learning Approach for Intrusion Detection System using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Network technology advancements have significantly increased the risk of device and data compromise, particularly during data sharing and distribution. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) based intrusion detection systems (IDS) present effective solutions for mitigating these threats. However, in networks with numerous devices, sharing data with a central server for model training poses serious privacy and security risks. Federated Learning (FL) presents a viable solution by eliminating the need to share data with the server for training. Instead, it enables local model training, with only model parameters transmitted to the server for aggregation in a continuous learning process. This paper addresses privacy and security challenges in intrusion detection by leveraging federated learning with Convolutional Neural Networks(CNN). The proposed approach is tested using the UNSW-NB15 dataset under both independent and identically distributed (IID) and non-independent and non-identically distributed (Non-IID) data distributions, providing competitive results compared to centralized architectures, while ensuring data privacy.

articleTitle: Enhanced Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy Based on Transfer Learning using DenseNet121
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a complication of diabetes that impacts the eyes. It damages the blood vessels of the light-sensitive tissue at the rear of the eye (retina). Initially, diabetic retinopathy may be asymptomatic or may produce mild vision problems. Nevertheless, it can lead to vision loss. Additionally, the decreasing ratio of ophthalmologists per population and the growing number of diabetes patients have extended waiting times for patients needing help. Thus, the early detection of diabetic retinopathy is more effective in facilitating diagnoses and preventing the progression of the illness to more severe stages. In recent years, deep learning has become a popular approach for enhancing performance in diverse fields, with a particular emphasis on medical image classification. Transfer learning models are extensively utilized as a deep learning technique and demonstrate considerable efficacy. This paper aims to use various deep-learning disciplines to detect diabetic retinopathy by employing specialized fundus imaging cameras. Our research is based on binary and quinary classification of DR with a handcrafted CNN model, transfer learning using DenseNet121, and this latter model in different tree-based algorithms and SVM classifiers. The proposed DenseNet121 model achieved better performance than other approaches with an accuracy of 99% on the binary and 81% on the quinary classifications. Finally, our model is compared with recent and pertinent research.

articleTitle: Measuring Cognitive Load in Children's Videos Using Motion Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Young children are particularly sensible to cognitive load, as the quantity and complexity of presented content significantly impact their learning capacity. To ensure a better learning experience, educational materials must be carefully designed to minimize cognitive overload. This study focuses on videos available on online streaming services that are targeted at children. A significant part of these videos is not created by educational experts, and a simple search can lead children to videos that may be cognitively overwhelming. This study aims to introduce a novel approach to assess the cognitive load of videos and, thus, determine their suitability for children by employing a motion detection approach. More precisely, we have implemented a block-matching motion detection approach to evaluate the overall motion present in a video. This approach was utilized to process a dataset of videos, facilitating the training of a classifier and the determination of a threshold that clearly separates high-motion videos from low-motion videos. The classifier has been used to develop a user-friendly tool designed to assist parents in evaluating videos before allowing their children to watch them.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Biometric System for Hand Dorsal Identification: Improving Accuracy and Robustness Through Tied-Rank Normalization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Biometric systems play a critical role in secure identity verification across various applications, yet existing modalities often face challenges related to hygiene, accuracy, and usability. This paper presents a novel hand dorsal biometric recognition system that leverages deep learning techniques and tied-rank normalization to enhance identification performance. Utilizing a dataset of 2,505 dorsal hand images from 500 individuals, our approach achieves an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 1.40% and a Recognition Rate (ROR) exceeding 94.8%. Performance evaluations through ROC and CMC analyses demonstrate the system's robustness and efficacy in distinguishing genuine users from imposters. Additionally, we explore the potential of multimodal fusion to further improve accuracy. Our findings indicate that hand dorsal biometrics is a promising solution for high-security environments, offering a contactless and hygienic alternative to traditional biometric systems.

articleTitle: Potato Disease Diagnosis with Symptoms Visualization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The devastating effects of global climate change on agricultural production have required regular monitoring of crops to detect possible diseases. Plant diseases are favored by the plants' stress, making them vulnerable to different environmental attacks. Herein, a new trend from artificial intelligence and computer vision emerges in crop monitoring; it involves tracking the health status of plants based on their morphological or physiological traits, the leaves being one of the plant constituents where diseases are mainly seen. In northern Africa, potatoes are a widely consumed food, and their harvest is a food security issue. This article addresses the detection and classification of potato diseases to allow early detection and treatment of diseases using a convolutional neural network based on potato leaf images. The deep learning-based models lack intrinsic explanation; this paper focuses particularly on the visualization aspect to address the results' explanation. The presented work addresses the explanation aspect of the decision by prospecting the feature maps in the convolutional layers and utilizing the Grad-CAM technique to visualize the detected symptoms that lead to the final decision through the classification layers.

articleTitle: Automated Machine Learning for Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using TPOT
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Breast cancer is a major global health issue, emphasizing the need for accurate diagnostic tools to improve patient outcomes. This paper presents an approach that utilizes Automated Machine Learning (AutoML), specifically the Tree-based Pipeline Optimization Tool (TPOT) Classifier, to streamline the model selection and so that optimizing breast cancer diagnosis process. The objective of the work is to develop a robust predictive model that classifies tumors as benign or malignant based on features derived from medical imaging data. The final model, a Random Forest Classifier, achieved an important accuracy score of 96.49%, demonstrating its effectiveness and reliability in clinical settings. Comprehensive evaluation metrics, including confusion matrix analysis and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve assessment, validate the model's performance, highlighting its potential for enhancing breast cancer diagnosis.

articleTitle: Exploring DeiT Transformers for Dermoscopic Image Classification: A Pilot Study
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Skin cancer is a significant public health concern, with millions of new cases diagnosed annually worldwide. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment and improved patient outcomes. Convolutional neural networks have shown promising results in skin cancer classification, but their performance can be limited by the availability of large, high-quality datasets. In this work, we present a novel approach for skin cancer diagnosis using the Data-efficient Image Transformer (DIET) architecture, which has demonstrated state-of-the-art performance on various image classification tasks.. The DeiT architecture is distinguished by its ability to capture long-range dependencies and contextual information, rendering it particularly adept at addressing complex visual patterns prevalent in dermatology. Furthermore, the DeiT model is optimized for performance on small datasets and with limited computational resources, owing to its efficient training methodology and knowledge distillation framework. We evaluate the DeiT model on the ISIC2019 dataset, which encompasses various skin lesion types, including melanoma. Our findings reveal an overall accuracy of 85%, accompanied by high precision and recall rates. These results underscore the potential of the DeiT transformer in advancing diagnostic capabilities in skin cancer diagnosis.

articleTitle: Using Deep Learning for Deadlock Detection in Intelligent Software Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This paper addresses deadlocks in concurrent software systems, presenting an AI-driven testing framework for detecting deadlocks in task interactions. Using advanced machine learning techniques, the system monitors task interactions, learns from historical data, and refines its detection ability. The approach formalizes task properties, such as states, resource demands, and dependencies, to build a robust interaction model. A supervised neural network algorithm provides real-time predictions, with evaluation metrics like detection accuracy and false positive rates for comparison with conventional methods. Results show significant improvements in deadlock detection accuracy, addressing scalability and manageability challenges faced by traditional solutions, offering a scalable AI alternative for modern distributed environments.

articleTitle: Automated Liver Segmentation Using 2D U-Net: A Deep Learning Approach for MRI Analysis and Surgical Planning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The liver's complexity in structure and function makes it susceptible to various forms of damage, highlighting the need for prompt and accurate diagnosis of liver tumors to ensure timely medical intervention. Image processing has emerged as a valuable tool for diagnostic support, especially in complex liver surgeries. This study presents a deep learning-based approach for automated liver segmentation on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) using a U-Net model. Our approach is designed to enhance preoperative planning by improving image analysis and aiding surgical teams in reducing potential complications. We utilized a public MRI dataset of 310 liver image series, representing diverse clinical cases and contrast types. Data augmentation techniques were applied to increase the model's robustness. After selecting the most suitable contrast type, we trained the U-Net model and evaluated its performance using metrics focused on segmentation accuracy. The model achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 94.37% and a 95th Percentile Hausdorff Distance (HD95) of 3.99 mm, demonstrating high precision in liver segmentations. These results emphasize the potential of this model as a reliable, MRI-based tool for clinical support in liver surgery planning and risk management.

articleTitle: Quantifying Explainability: Essential Guidelines for Evaluating XAI Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Deep Learning (DL) models have demonstrated excellence in executing complex tasks within sensitive fields such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems. However, ensuring that their decisions are understandable and trustworthy has become a critical concern. Explainable AI methods (XAI) have emerged to address this challenge by offering diverse techniques to explain how DL models arrive at their predictions. The increasing number of XAI methods, combined with their varied outputs, makes it challenging to assess which method is most suitable for a given task. In the literature, two main approaches have been proposed for evaluating XAI methods: qualitative and quantitative. In this paper, we focus on quantitative metrics and essential properties, such as faithfulness, robustness, and complexity, to effectively evaluate XAI methods. By analyzing these properties, we provide clear insight into the advantageous values, whether higher or lower. Additionally, to ensure consistency across metrics, we propose a new scores' transformation so that higher values consistently indicate better performance. This work serves as a comprehensive guide for practitioners and researchers, enabling them to select, assess, and improve explainability methods tailored to specific use cases.

articleTitle: Face Age Estimation: A Comparative Analysis of CNNs and Vision Transformers (ViTs)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Transformers have emerged as powerful models featuring self-attention mechanisms that dynamically weigh the significance of different input elements. While traditionally utilized in Natural Language Processing, their application in image classification remains relatively novel, with Convolutional Neural Networks historically dominating this domain. This study conducts a comparative analysis between Vision Transformers and Convolutional Neural Networks, specifically in the context of face age regression on the MORPH II dataset. By examining existing literature, we identify key architectural differences and performance metrics. Our experiments demonstrate that Vision Transformers outperform Convolutional Neural Networks in terms of accuracy and generalization ability, achieving a Mean Absolute Error of 3.44 compared to 4.85 for Convolutional Neural Networks. Furthermore, we analyze how dataset characteristics, image dimensions, and computational resources impact model performance. This work contributes to understanding the potential of Vision Transformers in image classification tasks, particularly in age estimation, and provides insights for future research in this evolving field.

articleTitle: Optimizing Research Laboratory Workflows in Algeria Through Low-Code BPMN Implementation with BonitaSoft
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This study presents the design and implementation of a digital workflow application specifically tailored for a scientific research laboratory at the Faculty of Computer Science, University of Biskra. Utilizing a Business Process Management (BPM) approach, the project aims to optimize and streamline laboratory processes, enhancing overall operational efficiency and performance. The workflow application is developed following Business Process Model and Notation 2 (BPMN 2.0) standards and implemented on the BonitaSoft low-code platform. Through systematic modeling of the laboratory's core processes, BPMN 2.0 provides a structured framework for effective workflow management and process improvement. BonitaSoft facilitates the development, deployment, and testing of these workflows, delivering a user-friendly interface and streamlined digital solution. The study concludes with an analysis of the application interfaces. It presents recommendations for future research, highlighting the potential for BPM tools in advancing laboratory management within scientific and academic environments.

articleTitle: NLP-Based Sentiment Analysis of the Palestinian-Israeli Conflict
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The resurgence of sentiment analysis (SA) has been driven by recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), making it a powerful tool for gauging public opinion across various domains. In light of the global attention surrounding the war in Gaza, this study applies and compares several natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze public sentiment expressed in social media comments about the conflict. A diverse range of classification approaches was explored, including traditional machine learning and deep learning approaches, as well as fine-tuning a transformer-based model, DistilBERT. The analysis revealed a predominance of negative sentiment in response to the war. Notably, the DistilBERT model outperformed other classifiers, achieving an accuracy of 89%, slightly ahead of the LSTM model at 88%. These results underscore the effectiveness of modern NLP techniques in sentiment analysis and provide valuable insights that can guide future research in this rapidly evolving field.

articleTitle: Smart Bracelet to Monitor Hospital Patients
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This research presents the development of an IoT-based smart bracelet designed to enhance healthcare monitoring by collecting real-time health data and precise 3D location (latitude, longitude, altitude) of patients. By transmitting this data to a central server, the bracelet enables the creation of a machine learning model capable of predicting patient outcomes, specifically recovery or mortality within a 28-day period. The model leverages advanced algorithms to process physiological and spatial data, providing healthcare providers with timely insights and enabling proactive care interventions. This study demonstrates the potential of IoT and machine learning to improve patient management, especially in critical care, by offering a predictive tool that supports informed clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: Paired Image to Image Translation for Ambient Occlusion Approximation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Screen space ambient occlusion seeks to accurately reproduce global illumination in real-time, thus rendering 3D scene details with smooth shadows. However, this method uses G-Buffers, which require multiple buffers to store the necessary information, which leads to some constraints, particularly regarding performance and memory management. This paper proposes a novel approach inspired by Screen space ambient occlusion, but using a single map. Moreover, ambient occlusion can be realistically simulated using generative models, such as image-to-image translation using deep neural networks. In this framework, we created a dataset of 10,000 synthetic images and developed a model to generate ambient occlusion efficiently. The suggested approach generates images similar to those created by classical methods, without the need for preprocessing or computation in the 3D space of the scene. The experimental results highlight the ability of our technique to generate high-quality and high-precision images.

articleTitle: Classification of Water Microorganisms using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Classification of water microorganisms is essential for maintaining water quality and protecting public health. Microbiological contamination poses serious challenges due to the diverse sizes, shapes, and morphologies of microorganisms, compounded by the inefficiency of traditional methods, which are often costly, labor-intensive, and time-consuming. This study addresses these issues by leveraging deep learning techniques, including Convolutional Neural Networks to accurately identify and classify microorganisms in water samples. Pre-trained models, such as Residual Network 50, Visual Geometry Group 19, and EfficientNet-B0, were integrated with Support Vector Machines to enhance classification performance. The methodology was implemented using Python and tools such as PyTorch, Scikit-learn, and OpenCV, with GPU acceleration enabled through CUDA and cuDNN. Evaluation metrics, including precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy, demonstrated outstanding performance, with results reaching precision, recall, and accuracy scores of up to 0.98. These findings highlight the effectiveness of advanced deep learning models in addressing the limitations of traditional approaches, offering a rapid, reliable solution for monitoring water quality and safeguarding public health.

articleTitle: Semantic Interoperability in Multi-Agent Planning: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This study examined the integration of Multi-Agent Planning (MAP) and semantic interoperability. It investigates how these two fields work together to improve the coordination, collaboration, and communication among autonomous agents in complex and ever-changing environments. Semantic interoper-ability provides a common language for agents that enhances mutual understanding and interaction. Conversely, distributed planning allows agents to make autonomous decisions while collaborating to achieve their common goals. The integration of these approaches offers promising opportunities for more effective coordination in comolex and decentralized systems

articleTitle: Using Geolocalized Social Network for Contact Tracing Based on Community Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Contact tracing is a method that traces infected people and then identifies all their contacts defined as potential new cases. In response to sudden outbreaks of epidemics, many contact tracing systems were proposed. Despite their efficiency, most of these systems are limited. While mobile applications require users' cooperation to install them, systems based on online social networks are more appropriate for communities active on online platforms. However, Google Maps with over twenty million downloads, has recently evolved into a social network in disguise where users share their opinions about the places they have visited. Thus, Google Maps data offer a good substitute for conventional contact tracking data. In this paper, we propose a novel approach applying a community detection algorithm to a social network built on Google Maps data. The proposed approach uses the Louvain algorithm to group both infected and safe people in communities, then identifies suspected cases based on resulted communities. Finally, the implementation of our approach shows its efficiency in covering more suspected cases compared to similar work.

articleTitle: Advanced Deep Learning Model for Improving Student Evaluation in Programming Education
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This paper investigates the potential applications of the pre-trained language model UniXcoder in programming education, with a focus on the utility of its embeddings in evaluating students' solutions. Due to its transformer-based architecture, UniXcoder is capable of generating syntactically and semantically meaningful code embeddings, enabling it to effectively understand and represent code patterns. The study employs these embeddings as input for predictive models to predict the correctness of student submissions. Using the Dublin introductory programming submission dataset (7,490 instances), Singapore dataset (4,393 instances), and Annaba dataset (87 instances), various machine learning models were compared. The primary contribution is the comparison of VniXcoder-based embeddings with traditional feature extraction methods. Results demonstrate that UniXcoder embeddings enhance prediction performance effectively, with the best model being the MLP with UniXcoder embeddings, achieving an accuracy of 96.06%, F1 score of 96.63%, Cohen's Kappa of 0.91, and ROC-AUC of 97.83% for the Dublin dataset. For the Singapore dataset, the MLP model achieved an accuracy of 87.71%, F1 score of 89.09%, Cohen's Kappa of 0.7504, and ROC-AUC of 92.73%. Additionally, the Balanced Bagging model on the Annaba dataset showed strong performance with an accuracy of 94.12%, F1 score of 95.24%, Cohen's Kappa of 0.8759, and ROC-AUC of 98.48%. These findings indicate that UniXcoder embeddings represent a promising approach for improving automated programming assessment.

articleTitle: Network Intrusion Detection System Using an Evolved Gene Regulatory Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The extensive inter-connectivity and interoperability of computing systems have become essential for fulfilling our daily activities. However, this increased connectivity has also led to larger attack surfaces and raised numerous security issues beyond human control, allowing malicious actors to exploit vulnerabilities in one system to compromise others more easily. Network intrusion detection is one of the security measures that counter evolving security threats to maintain secure communication. Adaptability and scalability are recognized issues in the development of network intrusion detection systems where many traditional machine learning systems may struggle to analyze large volumes of data in real time. For many years, biological complexity has been a source of inspiration for computer scientists. By modeling the underlying processes that drive this complexity, researchers aim to create systems capable of generating sophisticated behaviors, which can be leveraged for solving challenges in computer science and engineering. This paper introduces a novel bio-inspired model based on Gene Regulatory Networks as an alternative to traditional machine learning models for detecting and classifying network attacks. Our method shows results which are comparable to Machine Learning based methods when tested on UNSW-NB15 dataset, with an accuracy of 89.25% with a false positive rate of 3.81%.

articleTitle: Anxiety Recognition from Facial Expressions using Key Point Algorithm and Linear Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Recognizing human facial expressions and emotions is a fascinating and difficult topic. Facial expressions play a significant part in emotion perception and are employed in nonverbal communication between people. Facial expressions are crucial in everyday emotional communication since they are an indicator of sentiments and allow a person to convey his emotional state. People can instantly understand another person's emotional condition based on their facial expressions. As a result, information on facial expressions is frequently employed in automatic emotion recognition systems. Anxiety is one of the most prevalent emotions that people experience in various situations. As a result, it must be identified and treated. The goal of this work is to demonstrate an automated anxiety recognition system based on facial expressions employing key point techniques. SIFT, ORB, and SURF features are used to construct facial feature vectors from key point descriptors. The results revealed that using the Key Point feature significantly enhances the process of detecting face characteristics. The results indicate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithms, notably Shift technology. In summary, the Shift algorithm has the highest discrimination rate, although it takes longer to execute than other technologies.

articleTitle: Securing Fall Detection with Federated Learning: A Privacy-Centric Approach for IoT Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Efficient and automated fall detection is crucial in healthcare, especially for monitoring elderly individuals. Rapid and accurate systems can reduce response times, mitigating the risk of prolonged injuries or fatalities. However, ensuring the privacy of sensitive data remains a significant challenge. This paper presents a privacy-preserving fall detection framework that leverages federated learning and differential privacy to collaboratively train models while keeping sensitive data on-device. To assess its effectiveness, we evaluated the framework using four widely-used public datasets: MobiAct, UNIMIB, SisFAll, and FALLALLD. The results demonstrate its robust performance and adaptability across various scenarios. A comparative analysis with existing models highlights the framework's strong results, scalability, and suitability as a privacy-focused solution for real-world IoT healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Transformer-Based Approach for Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) have been used for years to protect enterprise hosts from cyberattacks. Traditional IDSs are usually based on simple methods, such as signatures or heuristics, that do not adapt to reactions against new threats that are constantly increasing. The objective of this paper is to develop an IDS based on a deep learning technique which is transformers. Unlike conventional models and thanks to their self-attention mechanism, transformers are characterized by an excellent ability to support complex patterns by very accurately modeling the context in sequential data. A host-based dataset containing system logs and network activities is used to train the transformer model that forms the core of the developed IDS. A detailed evaluation is used to compare our approach against existing methods based on machine learning and deep learning, showing significant improvements in precision, recall, and false positive rate. These results are very encouraging for developing robust IDSs that can be fine-tuned in real time to take into account new attacks.

articleTitle: Blockchain and Genetic Algorithms Interactions: A Brief Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The integration of Blockchain technology with genetic algorithms presents a novel approach to address complex optimisation challenges across various industries. This paper provides a comprehensive review about recent research on the hybridisation of Blockchain and genetic algorithms, focusing on applications that enhance system performance, scalability, and security. In the literature, Key contributions include energy optimisation in Blockchain-based systems, improved scalability through sharding techniques, and enhanced data integrity in healthcare systems. Additionally, genetic algorithms have been applied to optimise Blockchain adoption metrics, storage efficiency, and decentralised consensus mechanisms. Despite the promising results, challenges still remain such as high computational costs and scalability limitations. This review identifies these gaps and explores future research directions, particularly the potential of combining genetic algorithms with other artificial intelligence techniques and the development of adaptive consensus mechanisms. Our findings highlight the versatility and potential of genetic algorithm-enhanced Blockchain systems several areas such as energy management, e-commerce traceability, and decentralised decision-making, setting the stage for further exploration in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Next-Gen IoT Architecture: Long-Range, Low-Bandwidth Video Transmission Using GenAI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This paper introduces a groundbreaking IoT frame-work combining the Luckfox Pico Max RV1106 with LoRa (RYLR998) for low-bandwidth, long-range video transmission. The system integrates YOLOv5 Tiny for efficient edge processing, enabling real-time object detection and metadata generation directly on the Luckfox Pico Max RV1106. Detected metadata, including object, bounding box coordinates, confidence scores, is transmitted via LoRa to a central server. At the server, a large language model (LLM) processes the metadata to reconstruct a simulated visualization of the detected scene, offering a low-power alternative to full video transmission. The architecture demonstrates significant scalability, low energy consumption, and high reliability, making it ideal for remote surveillance, smart cities, and autonomous systems. By offloading computation to edge devices and utilizing LLM-based reconstruction, this approach showcases a transformative vision for future IoT networks emphasizing efficiency, scalability, and innovative data processing.

articleTitle: Parallel Whale Optimization Algorithm-Kmeans for Image Segmentation using Multiprocessing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Image segmentation is an important step in inter-preting and analyzing images, allowing computers and algorithms to process the content of an image accuratly and more effectively. Image segmentation is a crucial step in image preprocessing, while Kmeans is a widely-used clustering algorithm for im-age segmentation. However, the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is a nature-inspired metaheuristic optimization tech-nique known for its simplicity and global search capability. In this study, a hybrid approach was proposed, which combined WOA with Kmeans algorithm (WOA-Kmeans) to optimize image segmentation process, in the other hand, a parallel strategy was implemented for enhancing both segmentation quality and execution time. Traditional Kmeans suffers from sensitivity to initial cluster centroids, often leading to suboptimal results. By integrating WOA, the centroids initialization is improved, guiding Kmeans towards better convergence. Additionally, the parallelization of WOA-Kmeans using multiprocessing enables faster computation by distributing the work among multiple processes, making it suitable for high-resolution image processing tasks. This combination of WOA-Kmeans in a multiprocess environment ensures efficient and accurate image segmentation. The results demonstrate that the Parallel WOA-Kmeans outperform the sequentiel WOA-Kmeans in term of several performance measures, such as, accuracy, Root Mean Squar Error (RMSE), Peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR), and structural similarity index (SSIM).

articleTitle: CNN-Based Classification and Diagnosis of Alzheimer's from Baseline MRI Scans
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The diagnosis of neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's remains a medical challenge, relying heavily on physicians' interpretation of symptoms. Early detection and man-agement are critical for improving patient outcomes, but there is a lack of automated tools to assist in decision-making. This project aims to address this gap a framework for detecting Alzheimer's disease from MRI scans. A convolutional neural network (CNN) is used in the proposed method to classify images into four categories: No Dementia (ND), Very Mild Dementia (VMD), Mild Dementia (MD), and Moderate Dementia (MOD). Leveraging the proven capabilities of CNNs in medical image classification, a tailored architecture was designed and implemented. The model delivered strong performance, demonstrating its potential for early detection of Alzheimer's. This system could be used in clinical settings to assist physicians in identifying cases of Alzheimer's disease and improving diagnostic efficiency.

articleTitle: Facial Beauty Prediction Using Global Context Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Facial beauty prediction (FBP) has garnered significant attention in recent years due to its wide range of applications in cosmetics, entertainment, and healthcare. Traditional approaches rely heavily on handcrafted features or deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which often miss the global contextual information crucial for accurate prediction. This paper presents a novel method for facial beauty prediction using a Global Context Vision Transformer (GCViT). By leveraging the Vision Transformer's ability to model long-range dependencies and global relationships between facial features, our approach enhances the prediction accuracy beyond the limitations of CNN-based models. The proposed model integrates CNN-based feature extraction and Transformer-based attention mechanisms to effectively model intricate facial details and global context. A hierarchical architecture is used to progressively refine features across multiple resolutions, enabling the model to focus on fine-grained facial attributes while maintaining global consistency. We evaluate the performance of our model on the SCUT-FBP5500 dataset, achieving state-of-the-art results 0.9456 with significantly higher Pearson Correlation compared to existing methods. The experimental results demonstrate that the GC ViT outperforms traditional CNN-based approaches, offering a more effective solution for facial beauty prediction tasks.

articleTitle: Secure Consensus Mechanisms for Blockchained IoT: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The inherent security features of distributed ledger technologies can offer a promising solution to enhance the security of IoT systems, addressing their inevitable security concerns. Nonetheless, it is essential to consider potential flaws, particularly those related to consensus mechanisms within these blockchain-based IoT systems, to ensure the overall security and integrity of the network. Any threat at the blockchain level could potentially harm the entire IoT network. This paper investigates the security of the underlying consensus mechanisms within blockchain-based IoT systems. We present a review of securing consensus mechanisms within the Internet of Blockchained Things.

articleTitle: Enhanced EEG Classification via Riemannian Normalizing Flows and Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals present unique challenges for classification tasks due to their non-stationary and high-dimensional nature. In this paper, we propose a novel method that combines Riemannian geometry with deep learning to classify multi-class EEG data. Specifically, we compute covariance matrices of EEG signals and map them onto the tangent space of the Symmetric Positive Definite (SPD) manifold. A deep neural network architecture, termed NeuroSPDNet, is designed to effectively learn from these tangent space features. The method incorporates cross-validation for robust performance evaluation and utilizes Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) and Precision-Recall (PR) curves to assess classification effectiveness across four classes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves an overall accuracy of 96.23% with high precision and recall, significantly outperforming traditional approaches in EEG signal classification.

articleTitle: Combining Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain Technology in the Context of the Internet of Things (IoT) : A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The combination of Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and the Internet of Things (IoT) represents a transformational horizon in the field of information technology (IT). Blockchain delivers unrivaled security, immutability, and decentralization of systems, whereas AI provides powerful data analysis, learning capabilities, and intelligent decision-making skills, and integrating the two might have a significant positive influence on IoT. As the Internet of Things enables easy data interchange and communication between devices over the Internet, the integration of AI with blockchain opens up disruptive possibilities that could take the IoT to the next level. In this article, we investigate existing projects and their development in this arena, shining a focus on those who have already accepted and begun to execute this transformational concept.

articleTitle: A Diagnostic Classification Framework for Alzheimer's Disease: An Integrated Approach with ESIHE, SVM, and Wavelet Features
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is an irreversible neurodegenerative condition affecting the brain, resulting in cognitive decline, memory loss, and other neurological impairments, with no current cure or restorative treatment available. The primary objective of our study is to leverage machine learning (ML) methodologies for the precise and prompt identification of AD through medical images. The method utilizes structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) scans derived from the Kaggle dataset, encompassing four distinct classes: NonDemented (ND), VeryMildDemented (VMD), MildDemented (MD), and ModerateDemented (MoD). Our methodology employs Exposure-based sub-Image histogram equalization (ESIHE) for preprocessing, enhancing image quality for subsequent analysis. The feature extraction process utilizes Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to capture meaningful patterns from MR images. We proposed a classification based on Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm that involves two stages. In the first stage, three binary classifications were performed, while six binary classifications in the second stage. The automated classification achieved by our proposed model demonstrates compelling performance.

articleTitle: FedAGGEnsemble: a Federated Ensemble Learning based Approach for Malaria Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Malaria is one of the life-threatening diseases that is considered as a significant global health challenge, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. While various machine learning models have been proposed for malaria detection, a critical limitation is their reliance on centralized data, which often compromises patient privacy. To address this challenge, we introduce FedAGGEnsemble, a novel federated ensemble learning framework designed to enhance malaria detection accuracy while safeguarding data confidentiality. By leveraging the power of federated learning, our approach enables collaborative training of multiple local models on decentralized datasets, thereby preserving data privacy. The ensemble technique further improves predictive performance by combining the strengths of diverse models. Our experimental results demonstrate the superiority of FedAGGEnsemble over existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. This research underscores the potential of artificial intelligence to revolutionize public health and highlights the imperative of prioritizing data privacy in medical applications.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction through MS Lesion and Cerebral Lobe Segmentation for Enhanced EDSS Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: In this paper, we present a hybrid approach for segmenting multiple sclerosis (MS) lesions and predicting disability progression. Using Concat-UNet for accurate MS lesion segmentation and a multi-class UNet for brain lobe segmentation, we enable regional analysis of lesion impact. By fusing MRI, clinical, and demographic data, we enhanced EDSS prediction, with LightGBM achieving a high R2 score (0.96 ± 0.07)

articleTitle: Reward Function Analysis for Deep Reinforcement Learning Agent in Goal-Oriented Navigation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Designing a reward function is never a trivial task when implementing Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents. Instead, it is one of the most crucial steps for ensuring a stable and robust learner. This paper explores the impact of different reward function designs on the performance of a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) continuous control model. We investigate three distinct classes of reward functions: “Binary Class”, “Continuous Class” and “Sparse Class”, implemented to navigate a differential drive robot through unknown environments toward a designated goal without prior knowledge or pre-made maps, while avoiding obstacles. The designed reward functions are tested in two increasingly complex environments using the Gazebo simulator integrated with the Robot Operating System (ROS). Our study conducts a comparative analysis of these reward structures within the DRL framework to evaluate their influence on learning efficiency, reward variance, and agent stability. The findings reveal significant differences in learning behaviors and performance metrics across the reward types, providing insights into optimal reward structuring for enhancing DRL implementations in robotics. This work not only contributes to the theoretical understanding of reward design in RL but also offers practical guidance for developing more effective DRL systems in robotic applications.

articleTitle: Combining Model Checking and Spectrum-Based Fault Localization with Multiple Counterexamples
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: In the realm of software debugging, fault localization is a critical and challenging task. Traditional methods, including spectrum-based techniques and model checking, have demonstrated varying degrees of success but are limited by their inherent constraints. In this paper, we present a novel advancement in fault localization accuracy by integrating spectrum-based techniques with model checking, leveraging multiple counterexamples. Our previous work introduced this combined approach using a single counterexample; however, in this study, we show that utilizing multiple counterexamples significantly enhances the accuracy of fault localization. Experimental evaluations on the TCAS benchmark from the Siemens test suite demonstrate an average improvement of 62.80% in fault localization accuracy compared to traditional spectrum-based techniques, with a 20.39% increase when using multiple counterexamples versus a single one. This advancement underscores the potential of leveraging multiple counterexamples to improve the precision of fault localization.

articleTitle: Intelligent Telecom Solutions: Employing Large Language Models to Address Base Station Anomalies and Alarm Prioritization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Telecom network issues disrupt critical services and lead to substantial financial losses. This study focuses on two key tasks: generating solutions for Base Station (BS) problems and prioritizing BS alarms using Large Language Models (LLMs). The application of these models improves telecom network management by reducing downtime and increasing reliability during emergencies. Six LLMs were evaluated: Mixtral, Llama, and Gemini for generating solutions. DistilBERT, DistilGPT-2, and ELECTRA for alarm prioritization. Mixtral achieved a high cosine similarity score of 0.9647, outperforming Llama, Gemini, and traditional models such as Markov in resolving BS anomalies. DistilBERT demonstrated superior accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score in classifying alarm priorities for BS compared to DistilGPT-2, ELECTRA, and conventional models such as SVM and Naive Bayes. These findings highlight the potential of LLMs to significantly improve stability and reliability in the telecommunications industry, providing valuable advances over traditional methods.

articleTitle: Using FER+ Dataset to Implement Deep Capsule Network for Facial Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The researchers have been directed to use the fresh dataset known as the Facial Emotion Recognition Plus (FER+) Dataset. This has enhanced the efficacy of conventional facial recognition technologies, particularly in analyzing human facial expressions. Consequently, it is essential to improve the existing generation of facial recognition systems to accommodate diverse datasets. The current generation of facial recognition technology predominantly depends on deep learning, which presents challenges due to the inadequacy of existing facial databases. The current study proposes the implementation of the Deep Capsule Network and Light Gradient Boosting Machine algorithms utilizing FER+ to develop a system for recognizing facial emotions. This facial database is accessible at no cost for scholarly purposes and was employed to categorize the available images showcasing a range of facial emotions, aligning with one of the seven fundamental human facial expressions, thereby facilitating the development of more sophisticated facial technology. Following our research findings, the proposed facial emotion detection achieves an accuracy of up to 88.92% owing to its meticulously curated facial database.

articleTitle: Formal Specification, and Verification of a Cooperative Multi-robots System for Delivery Service
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The growing demand for efficient delivery services, especially in regions with infrastructure challenges, has led to the emergence of multi-robot systems as a potential solution. This paper introduces a formal specifying and verifying of a cooperative multi-robots system specifically developed for delivery services. The approach encompasses both the design of a delivery robot prototype and a rigorous formal specification framework to ensure robust coordination and safety. Using Büchi automata and UPPAAL model-checking tool, the system's safety and liveness properties which are represented by computational tree logic (CTL) were validated, demonstrating reliable navigation and task performance in dynamic environments. The results confirm the system's potential for enhancing delivery operations, providing a scalable, verifiable model suited for real-world deployment.

articleTitle: Facial Marks as Biometric Indicators for Celebrity Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The widespread availability of celebrity images and videos online has driven significant advancements in training deep neural networks for celebrity face recognition. While deep learning excels in analyzing complex visual attributes such as identity, age, gender, and race, the internal mechanisms governing these models remain largely opaque. In contrast, human visual processing is guided by well-established biological principles, utilizing saccadic eye movements to efficiently gather detailed information from salient regions in the visual field. This process leverages the retina's varied resolution and retino-cortical mapping, enabling simultaneous broad scene comprehension and precise detail capture. Inspired by these principles, this paper introduces a novel face analysis system that integrates the HMAX model―a biologically-plausible, hierarchical visual architecture―with a log-polar image representation, which simulates early-stage visual processing in primates. The proposed system employs a space-variant sampling method that enhances context awareness by combining peripheral, low-resolution visual information with high-resolution details from central visual regions. This design enables effective identification and analysis of both coarse structural features (e.g., face shape) and fine-grained details (e.g., scars, moles, wrinkles) critical for robust face recognition. By bridging biological insights with state-of-the-art computational techniques, the proposed approach offers a promising path toward more interpretable and efficient visual analysis models.

articleTitle: Individuality Within Crowd: Distinctive Features to Ensure a Diverse Crowd Appearance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Crowds are a significant part of our daily lives, representing numerous individuals who appear in a specific place, each engaging in various activities as part of their daily routines. We notice that each individual has a distinctive appearance that distinguishes them, such as their clothing color, skin color, eye color, and hairstyle. Each individual is characterized by wearing distinct accessories. We also observe variations in shape and height. In this paper, we present a crowd composed of numerous characters, each with distinct appearance traits to ensure individuality. First, we introduced a range of concepts to enhance the diversity of appearances. This step involved incorporating a variety of features, including variations in eye and hair colors, textures for clothing and accessories, the addition of different accessories, as well as variations in height and body shape. Second, we evaluated the efficacy of our approach by calculating the total number of combinations of these elements. The results demonstrate that our model enhances both the realism and visual diversity of the crowd. By utilizing these sets, it significantly improves the overall appearance, resulting in a more varied and realistic representation of the crowd.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enabled Car Market in Algeria: A Hyperledger Fabric Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The car market is a complex system. It involved a vast amount of information, from vehicle details and ownership history to maintenance records and market trends. Thus, it necessitates robust information technology systems for effective management. The car market is vulnerable to fraudulent activities such as odometer tampering, fake history reports, stolen vehicle sales, paperwork hassle, parts counterfeiting, and unclear ownership trails. In this paper, we propose a modular architecture for implementing Hyperledger Fabric in the car market of Algeria. The use of Blockchain technology on the Fabric Ledger platform will enable private tracking, monitoring, and control of car exchanges, which could potentially be utilized by authorities in managing Algeria's car markets. Our proposed architecture was implemented in the Hyperledger Fabric framework. Performance evaluation included measuring chaincode metrics (request duration, request reception, and completion), endorser metrics (successful proposal duration, proposal received, successful proposals), and ledger metrics (block processing and storage commit time, statedb commit time, Blockchain height).

articleTitle: AI-Driven Insights into the Relationship Between Psychological State and Academic Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This paper presents an experiment on the application of AI, specifically machine learning techniques, to advance psychological research and practice. The study investigates the relationship between the psychological state of computer scienc students and their academic performance. Using a guided survey, a local dataset was created with 265 students and 31 variables. This dataset was then used to train AI models aimed at predicting academic performance based on selected input factors. While some traditional machine learning algorithms demonstrated relatively low accuracy, the application of the Random Forest algorithm with SMOTE(Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) significantly improved predictive accuracy. These promising results highlight the potential of AI to support and accelerate research in psychology, enhancing both study precision and experimental efficacy.

articleTitle: Retinopathy Lesions Segmentation Using YOLOv9 and Grad-CAM: An Advanced Approach for Disease Grading and Localization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of blindness, and accurate detection and segmentation of retinal lesions are critical for effective diagnosis and treatment. This paper presents an automated approach for DR lesion segmentation using the YOLOv9 model, combined with Grad-CAM for interpretability. YOLOv9 was chosen for its advanced object detection capabilities, enabling effective localization of small lesions, while Grad-CAM provides heatmaps for better interpretability, making it easier to understand the model's focus areas during prediction. The proposed method was evaluated on two public datasets, DDR and IDRiD, achieving high segmentation accuracy across various lesion types, including microaneurysms (MAs), hemorrhages (HE), exudates (EX), and soft exudates (SE). For DDR, the model achieved mean Average Precision (mAP) scores of 0.769 for MAs, 0.917 for HEs, 0.843 for EX, and 0.960 for SE at an IoU threshold of 0.5, with an overall mAP of 0.872 across all classes. The precision-recall curve and normalized confusion matrix further demonstrated the model's high recall and precision, especially for hemorrhages and soft exudates, while microaneurysms showed slightly lower precision due to background misclassifications. This approach combines high detection accuracy with interpretability, making it a promising tool for aiding ophthalmologists in DR diagnosis. Future work will focus on refining lesion detection for challenging classes and exploring multi-modal data integration for broader retinal disease applications.

articleTitle: Paludism Detection using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This study introduces a convolutional neural network (CNN) approach for diagnosing malaria (paludism) using a hybrid dataset, integrating 27,558 images from public sources with 442 locally-collected samples from southern Algeria to ensure the model's relevance for regional healthcare applications. We compared our CNN architecture against popular transformer-based models, VGG19 and VGG16, as well as an earlier CNN architecture. While VGG19 and VGG16 are renowned for their performance in medical imaging, our older CNN architecture outperformed both, achieving an accuracy of 99.85%, specificity of 99.92%, and sensitivity of 99%. This model's robust performance across diverse blood smear images, including regional variations, positions it as an effective diagnos-tic tool tailored to local needs, supporting healthcare providers in accurately identifying malaria infections.
